title: ALTER TABLE ADD Column
description: Learn how to add one or more columns to an existing table using ALTER TABLE ADD.

data.text: SQL Server ALTER TABLE ADD Column
The ALTER TABLE ADD statement appends a new column to an existing table. You can add a single column or multiple columns in one statement.

data.title: Add a Single Column
data.content: Adds one column to an existing table.
data.code:
ALTER TABLE table_name
ADD column_name data_type column_constraint;

data.title: Add Multiple Columns
data.content: Adds multiple columns to an existing table in one statement.
data.code:
ALTER TABLE table_name
ADD
    column_name_1 data_type_1 column_constraint_1,
    column_name_2 data_type_2 column_constraint_2,
    ...
    column_name_n data_type_n column_constraint_n;

data.text: Note that SQL Server does not support adding a column after an existing column as MySQL does. New columns are always appended to the end of the table.
The following example creates a quotations table and then adds columns to it.

data.title: Create Quotations Table
data.content: Creates the quotations table for demonstration.

data.title: Add a Single Column
data.content: Adds a description column to the quotations table.
data.code:
ALTER TABLE sales.quotations
ADD description VARCHAR (255) NOT NULL;

data.title: Add Multiple Columns
data.content: Adds amount and customer_name columns to the quotations table.
data.code:
ALTER TABLE sales.quotations
    ADD
        amount DECIMAL (10, 2) NOT NULL,
        customer_name VARCHAR (50) NOT NULL;

data.title: ALTER TABLE ADD Key Points
points: Use ALTER TABLE ADD to append new columns to an existing table.
You can add a single column or multiple columns in one statement.
New columns are always appended to the end of the table in SQL Server.
Specify data types and constraints (NOT NULL, DEFAULT, etc.) for each new column.
